name: Sale, VAT 12.5 %
description: A taxable supply made in Saint Lucia by a taxable person, standard-rated
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 9(1)(a) and s. 10(1) — value added tax on every taxable supply by a taxable person at 12.5 % (the 15 % of the 2012 enactment replaced by S.I. 101 of 2016, in force 1 February 2017, which is the valid_from; the revised text of s. 10 on the Attorney General's Chambers site shows 12.5 %). The tax is accounted for by the supplier (s. 9(2)(a)) and enters the net tax of s. 29. The base posts to box 1 net of the tax, the tax to box 7 (box numbers are this pack's, see tax_report.json).

name: Retail sale, VAT 12.5 %, the price includes the tax
description: A standard-rated sale whose price already holds the VAT
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 10(1) at 12.5 %, with the tax extracted from a price that includes it — what price_include does: 112.50 holds 100.00 and 12.50. Same boxes as LC-S-12.5.

name: Sale of restaurant food and beverages, water sports, tours and attractions, VAT 10 %
description: Food and beverages of a restaurant, water sports, tours and admission to heritage sites and tourist attractions
legal_reference: Value Added Tax (Rate of Tax) (Tourism Sector Goods and Services) Order, 2020 (S.I. 188 of 2020), made under s. 10(2) of the Act, in force 1 December 2020, art. 3(b) — ten per cent on food and beverages, alcoholic beverages included, supplied by a restaurant; water sports; tours by land, air or sea within Saint Lucia (including the tour operator's own transport as part of the package, but not transport it buys in); and admission to heritage sites and other tourist attractions. The pack does not decide which supplies qualify. Base to box 2, tax to box 8.

name: Sale of tourism accommodation, VAT 7 %
description: The supply of a tourism accommodation service: sleeping accommodation in the tourism sector, with or without related facilities
legal_reference: Value Added Tax (Rate of Tax) (Tourism Sector Goods and Services) Order, 2020 (S.I. 188 of 2020), art. 2 and 3(a) — seven per cent on a supply of a tourism accommodation service, "the supply of a service for sleeping accommodation in the tourism sector with or without related facilities for consideration". The Order revokes the earlier hotel order of 2014. Base to box 3, tax to box 9.

name: Zero-rated supply (export)
description: An export of goods or services, zero-rated
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 16 and First Schedule, para. 2(1)(a) and (b) (goods entered for export and exported, with the documentary proof the Comptroller accepts, s. 16(4) and para. 3) and para. 2(2)(a) to (d) (services connected with land abroad, supplied to a non-resident, to a free zone business or to a foreign telecommunication carrier) — zero per cent. A zero-rated supply is a taxable supply: the input tax of what produces it stays deductible (s. 30), and s. 57(5) lets a person whose supplies are half zero-rated claim the excess at once. Base to box 4.

name: Zero-rated supply in Saint Lucia
description: A domestic supply of the First Schedule at zero per cent (fuel, water and sewerage, electricity, fresh eggs, uncooked pasta, live animals other than pets)
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 16 and First Schedule, para. 2(1)(g), (h), (j), (k) and 2(2)(e), (f) — zero per cent on live animals other than pets, fuel (the customs tariff headings of para. 1), fresh eggs and uncooked pasta, ventilated boxes for agricultural produce, water and sewerage supplied by the Saint Lucia Water and Sewerage Company and electricity supplied by Saint Lucia Electricity Services Limited. The Schedule is amended by Order (for instance the temporary zero-rating of building materials) and the pack does not follow the amendments: the user checks the item against the current Schedule. Base to box 4.

name: Exempt supply
description: A supply of the Second Schedule (financial services, medical services, education, residential sale and rent, lotteries), outside the tax
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 17 and Second Schedule, para. 2 — exempt supplies include financial services, medical services other than cosmetic ones, care of the aged and disabled, education services and supplies, the sale of a dwelling and its rental, agricultural land, and games of chance run by non-profit organisations and lotteries. A supply that would be zero-rated is not exempt (s. 17(3)). The input tax of what is acquired to make an exempt supply is not deductible (s. 30). Base to box 5.

name: Purchase, VAT 12.5 %
description: A purchase from a taxable person, standard-rated, with a tax invoice
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 29(1) and s. 30(1)(a) — the tax payable is the output tax less the input tax deduction allowed, which covers the tax on taxable supplies made to the person for use in a taxable activity, on a tax invoice (s. 34) or a tax credit or debit note (s. 35). Section 31 denies the deduction for passenger vehicles, entertainment and the like, and s. 30 allocates a mixed use: both are the user's. Base to box 12, tax to box 14.

name: Purchase of restaurant, water sport, tour or attraction services, VAT 10 %
description: A purchase of the tourism services taxed at ten per cent
legal_reference: Value Added Tax (Rate of Tax) (Tourism Sector Goods and Services) Order, 2020 (S.I. 188 of 2020), art. 3(b), and Act s. 30 — input tax at ten per cent is deductible on the same conditions as at 12.5 %. Base to box 12, tax to box 14.

name: Purchase of tourism accommodation, VAT 7 %
description: A purchase of tourism accommodation taxed at seven per cent
legal_reference: Value Added Tax (Rate of Tax) (Tourism Sector Goods and Services) Order, 2020 (S.I. 188 of 2020), art. 3(a), and Act s. 30 — input tax at seven per cent is deductible on the same conditions as at 12.5 %. Base to box 12, tax to box 14.

name: Import of goods, VAT 12.5 %
description: Import of goods, VAT paid to the Comptroller of Customs
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 9(1)(b), s. 10(1) and s. 22 to 25 — 12.5 % of the value of a taxable import of goods, paid to the Comptroller of Customs on the import; the value for tax (s. 22 and following) includes duty and freight, which the pack does not compute: it applies 12.5 % to the invoice value and the customs entry is the user's. The tax paid is deductible (s. 30(1)(a)). Base to box 11, tax to box 13.

name: Purchase without VAT
description: A purchase of a zero-rated or exempt supply, or from a person not registered
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 15.42 (Act No. 7 of 2012), s. 16, s. 17 and the First and Second Schedules — a zero-rated supply carries tax at zero per cent and an exempt supply none, so the purchaser has no input tax to deduct; the value is still reported among the purchases of the period (box 12).
